global_briefing: The Trump, Xi and Putin APEC-linked summit produced a peace declaration whose meaning is disputed. A calmer US-China trade track lowers copper tariff risk, but China's licence terms for antimony, tungsten and rare earths are still open. Trump says the US will "see what happens" with Iran after January 1, and Hormuz disruption would hit diesel and sulphur costs first. Ukraine keeps munitions demand firm for tungsten and antimony. The IMF warns global debt is near 100% of GDP, which squeezes critical-minerals budgets and junior finance. El Niño brings water and power stress to the Andes and Australia, and Mongolia's presidential resignation adds policy risk at Oyu Tolgoi.
